errorCodes.meaning: The install token is missing, malformed, expired or already consumed, or the claim code does not match it. Deliberately one code for all of these, so an unauthenticated start is no oracle for which half was wrong.
The install token was issued for a passkey claim and names no administrator DID. Claim it with vtc/install/claim/passkey/start, or have the operator issue a token naming the founder's DID.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

adminDid.description: The DID the install token names — the DID that must sign claim/finish and that becomes the first administrator. Returned so the installer need not decode the token.

audience.description: The community's DID, which the statement names as its `audience` and `recipient`, and to which claim/finish is addressed.

challenge.description: A fresh challenge (≥128 bits) the founder's step-up approver signs over in its auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1 statement with `purpose: enrol`.

claimId.description: Opaque, single-use handle for this claim. Echoed in claim/finish, and the `boundTo` of the approver's enrolment statement.

expiresAt.description: When this claim ceremony lapses (not the install token).

Response.title: VTC Install Claim Start — response payload

schema.description: Begin claiming a fresh community under a DID the founder already controls: exchange the install token and its claim code for a challenge the founder's step-up approver will sign. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

claimCode.description: The claim code the operator received out of band, through a different channel from the install URL. Required in 0.3. Compared with its stored hash; never logged.

token.description: The EdDSA-signed install JWT (aud=vtc-install) printed by vtc setup. In 0.3 it names the founder's DID.
